title: Entropy as First Principle: Deriving Quantum and Gravitational Structure from Thermodynamic Geometry
content: This paper introduces the Total Entropic Quantity (TEQ) framework, a structural reformulation of quantum theory grounded in two foundational axioms. Axiom 0 posits entropy as a generative constraint: a geometric principle that determines which configurations can stably distinguish themselves, independent of space, time, or dynamics. Here, entropy refers to a curvature-functional over distinguishability configurations, maintaining only those structural patterns that remain stable or well-posed under finite informational resolution—that is, structures that are not destroyed or dissolved by coarse-graining or limited observability. Axiom 1, the Minimal Principle (MP), selects from these configurations those that remain maximally resolvable under finite entropy resolution. From this entropic foundation, core features of quantum theory—including the Born rule, Schrödinger dynamics, quantization, and gravitational structure—emerge as consequences of variation within an entropy-curved geometry. TEQ unifies quantum coherence, classical emergence, and spacetime curvature under a single informational principle, replacing conventional postulates with entropy-stabilized structure. The framework predicts deviations in high-curvature regimes and reinterprets physical law as the geometry of distinguishability rather than imposed dynamics.
